header.userPrompt:
Implement GitHub issue #83 in AlexITC/expense-tracker: improve the expense dedup flow to detect orphaned row-less duplicates and add bulk dedup with per-row checkboxes. Full spec follows.

## Problem

The expense dedup flow only handles one shape of duplicate: a row-linked expense (survivor) paired with a receipt-bearing, row-less expense (loser). See `web/.../utils/ExpenseDuplicateDetector.scala` (survivor = `rowIds.nonEmpty && receiptIds.isEmpty`, loser = `rowIds.isEmpty` and has a receipt).

This misses a second, common shape: **orphaned duplicates left after deleting a duplicate bank statement.** When the same statement was imported twice and one copy is deleted, that copy's expenses lose their row and become row-less with **no receipt**. Each one duplicates a surviving row-linked expense (same amount, same date, same merchant), but because the orphan has no receipt it is neither a survivor nor a loser under the current rules, so the UI never surfaces it. A real cleanup produced dozens of such orphans and the UI flagged none of them.

## Goal

1. **Detect orphan duplicates.** Extend the detector to also pair a row-linked survivor with a row-less, receipt-less twin (same amount, date within the existing window, merchant for the Strong tier). For this shape the orphan carries nothing to fold in, so the "merge" degenerates to deleting the orphan; the surviving row-linked expense already holds the real data (splits stay with it).

2. **Bulk dedup.** Add a checkbox on each duplicate candidate row plus a bulk action button, so a large batch (the orphan case produces many at once) can be processed in one go instead of one dialog at a time. Selecting rows and clicking the bulk button resolves all selected candidates. Keep the per-candidate action too.

## Notes

- Preserve the existing receipt-vs-row behavior unchanged; this adds a case, it does not replace one.
- Keep the ambiguity handling: when an expense appears in more than one candidate, it still needs review, so a bulk run must not silently resolve ambiguous candidates without the user picking the right partner. Decide how bulk interacts with ambiguous pairs (e.g. bulk applies only to unambiguous Strong candidates; ambiguous ones stay manual).
- The two merge shapes differ: receipt-vs-row moves a receipt onto the survivor; orphan-vs-row just deletes the orphan. The bulk path must do the right one per candidate.
- All user-owned queries scoped by `user_id`.

resultJson.description:
The duplicates panel on the expenses page currently finds only one kind of duplicate. A bank-row expense (the survivor: has a row, no receipt) is paired with a hand-entered expense that has a receipt but no row (the loser), and the merge moves the receipt onto the survivor. It misses orphans: row-less expenses with no receipt that are left behind when a duplicate bank statement is deleted. Each orphan has the same amount, a date within the window, and usually the same merchant as a surviving row-linked expense, but no current rule matches it. One real cleanup left dozens of them and none were flagged.

This epic adds the orphan shape end to end and leaves the receipt shape working exactly as it does now. On the server, `POST /expenses/:id/merge` accepts a loser with no row and no receipt. In that case it just moves refunds to the survivor and deletes the loser. It only allows keepDetailsFrom=Row, and the existing guards stay in place: user scoping, survivor must have a row, loser must have no row. Reusing the merge endpoint instead of plain delete means the server checks the pair's shape and keeps any refunds on the orphan. On the web side, `ExpenseDuplicateDetector` also pairs row-linked survivors with receipt-less, row-less twins. The panel and confirm dialog say "delete the duplicate" for these rather than "move the receipt". Ambiguity is still counted across both shapes together.

Last, the panel gets per-candidate checkboxes and a bulk action, so a large batch can be cleared in one confirmed step. Bulk only works on unambiguous Strong candidates. Weak and ambiguous candidates have no checkbox and stay one-at-a-time. Every bulk item calls the same merge endpoint with keepDetailsFrom=Row; the only per-shape difference is local state (a receipt candidate also records its moved receipt on the survivor). The per-candidate buttons stay.

tasks.title: Server: allow merging a receipt-less orphan (merge = delete orphan)
tasks.description: Extend `ExpensesRepository.merge` / `validateMerge` (server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/ExpensesRepository.scala) so a loser with NO receipt is accepted. Keep the existing guards: SelfMerge, ExpenseNotFound (both looked up with userId), SurvivorWithoutRow, LoserWithRow. Change `ValidatedMerge.receipt` to `Option[Receipt]`. When the loser has a receipt, behave exactly as today: the SurvivorWithReceipt guard applies, the receipt is relinked, and keepDetailsFrom=Receipt adopts details. When the loser has no receipt: skip the SurvivorWithReceipt guard and the receipt relink; reject keepDetailsFrom=Receipt with a new `MergeError` case (e.g. `OrphanDetailsNotSupported("Cannot keep the duplicate's details because it has no receipt")`); still run `RefundDAO.reassignExpense` and `ExpenseDAO.delete(loserId, userId)` in the same transaction. Remove the now-unused `LoserWithoutReceipt` case if nothing else uses it. Update the class/method doc comments. Add tests to server/src/test/scala/controllers/ExpensesControllerSpec.scala under "POST /expenses/:id/merge": (1) an orphan merge with Row deletes the orphan, keeps the survivor's row, splits and merchant, and leaves the survivor's receipt list unchanged; (2) an orphan merge works even when the survivor already has a receipt; (3) an orphan merge with Receipt fails with the new message and deletes nothing; (4) an orphan owned by another user fails with "Expense not found". Reuse the `linkToNewRow` / `createLinkedReceipt` helpers. Verify with `sbt "testOnly controllers.ExpensesControllerSpec"`.

tasks.title: Web: detect orphan duplicates and render/merge them correctly
tasks.description: In web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/utils/ExpenseDuplicateDetector.scala, change `Candidate.receiptId: UUID` to `receiptId: Option[UUID]` (None = orphan shape). In `detect`, keep the receipt pairs unchanged (survivor: rowIds.nonEmpty && receiptIds.isEmpty; loser: rowIds.isEmpty with a receipt). Add orphan pairs: survivor is any expense with rowIds.nonEmpty (it may already have a receipt), loser has rowIds.isEmpty && receiptIds.isEmpty, amounts are exactly equal, and dates are within `ReconciliationMatcher.MaxDateDifferenceDays`. Use the same `tierFor`. Compute ambiguity counts over the union of both pair lists. Keep the ordering, and update the scaladoc to describe both shapes. Update the callers. In ExpensesPage.scala `handleMerge`, only call `setMergedReceipts` when `receiptId` is defined. In ExpenseDuplicatesPanel.scala, for orphan candidates: title the loser column "Duplicate (no receipt)" instead of "Receipt"; hide "View receipt" and "Merge, keep receipt details"; replace "Merge, keep row details" with a single "Delete duplicate" button that calls `onMerge(c, MergeDetailsSource.Row)`. Keep Dismiss. Use the matching column title in `columns`. In ExpensesPage.scala, make `mergeSummary` (and the dialog title or button label if useful) say the orphan has no receipt and will be deleted, and that the bank-row expense keeps its details. Tests: ExpenseDuplicateDetectorSpec (orphan pairs, Strong vs Weak, out-of-window and different-amount rejection, survivor with a receipt still pairs with an orphan, a survivor matching both an orphan and a receipt loser is ambiguous, the existing receipt cases are unchanged with `Some(receiptId)`); ExpenseDuplicatesPanelSpec (an orphan candidate shows "Delete duplicate", sends Row, and has no keep-receipt button); fix ExpensesPageSpec for the new field type. Verify with `sbt "testOnly *ExpenseDuplicateDetectorSpec *ExpenseDuplicatesPanelSpec *ExpensesPageSpec"`.

tasks.title: Web: bulk dedup with per-candidate checkboxes
tasks.description: Add bulk resolution to the duplicates panel. Add a pure eligibility rule, `ExpenseDuplicateDetector.isBulkEligible(c: Candidate): Boolean = c.tier == Tier.Strong && !c.ambiguous`. Keep selection state in `ExpenseList` (ExpensesPage.scala) as `Set[String]` of `ExpenseList.dismissKey(c)`. Derive the effective selection each render as selected keys ∩ the keys of current eligible `duplicateCandidates`, so merged, dismissed, or now-ambiguous candidates drop out on their own. Extend `ExpenseDuplicatesPanel` Props with `selected: Set[String]`, `onToggleSelected: (Candidate, Boolean) => Unit`, `onToggleAll: Boolean => Unit` and `onBulkMerge: () => Unit`. Eligible cards show a `mui.Checkbox` (pattern: BankStatementReviewRow.scala:244, `.checked(...).size("small").onChange((_, checked) => ...)`). Ineligible cards show no checkbox; ambiguous ones keep their hint. The panel header gets a select-all checkbox (checked / indeterminate over the eligible candidates) and a "Merge selected (N)" contained button, disabled when N = 0. Keep the per-candidate buttons. Clicking bulk opens a confirm `mui.Dialog` in ExpensesPage. It shows the count, explains that receipts move to their bank-row expense, that duplicates without a receipt are deleted, and that bank-row details are kept, and says the action cannot be undone. On confirm, run the merges one after another (chain Futures with foldLeft) with `MergeDetailsSource.Row`. After each success, use functional updates: `setDeletedIds(_ + loser.id)`, plus `setMergedReceipts(_ + (survivor.id -> r))` when `receiptId` is `Some(r)`. Collect failures and report them through `setError` with a count and the first message. Clear the selection at the end. Factor the single-merge state update so `handleMerge` and the bulk path share it. Tests: ExpenseDuplicateDetectorSpec for `isBulkEligible`; ExpenseDuplicatesPanelSpec (checkboxes only on eligible candidates, toggling a checkbox calls `onToggleSelected`, select-all calls `onToggleAll`, the bulk button is disabled with no selection and calls `onBulkMerge` when enabled); a pure helper test in ExpensesPageSpec if the effective-selection logic is factored into `ExpenseList`. Verify with targeted `testOnly` for those specs.

resultJson.brief:
Layers: Tapir endpoints and models live in lib/api/shared (shared by both sides). The Play server goes controller → action → repository → DAO (Anorm). The Scala.js frontend (Slinky + MUI 5) is in web/.

Key files:
- web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/utils/ExpenseDuplicateDetector.scala: pure detector. `enum Tier { Strong, Weak }`, `case class Candidate(survivor: GetExpenses.Response.Expense, loser: GetExpenses.Response.Expense, receiptId: UUID, tier: Tier, ambiguous: Boolean)`, `def detect(expenses: List[Expense]): List[Candidate]`. The date window is `ReconciliationMatcher.MaxDateDifferenceDays`. Amounts must be exactly equal (BigDecimal ==). Strong means both merchantIds are defined and equal. A candidate is ambiguous when its survivor or loser appears in more than one pair. Output is sorted by (-survivor.date, survivor.id, loser.id).
- `GetExpenses.Response.Expense` fields: id, amount, date: LocalDate, time, merchantId: Option[UUID], merchantName, notes: Option[String], splits, createdAt, receiptIds: List[UUID], rowIds: List[UUID]. receiptIds and rowIds default to Nil, as the panel spec relies on.
- web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/expenses/ExpenseDuplicatesPanel.scala: candidate cards grouped by tier. `columns(c, categories)` and `column(title, e, categories)` are public and are also used by the merge dialog. Buttons: "View receipt" (only when receiptFilenames has the receiptId; calls ctx.api), "Merge, keep row details" / "Merge, keep receipt details" → `onMerge(c, MergeDetailsSource.Row|Receipt)`, and "Dismiss". Each card is keyed by `ExpenseList.dismissKey(c)` = s"${survivor.id}:${loser.id}".
- web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/expenses/ExpensesPage.scala: the `ExpenseList` component owns all state. deletedIds: Set[UUID], mergedReceipts: Map[survivorId → receiptId], adoptedDetails, dismissed: Set[String], pendingMerge: Option[(Candidate, MergeDetailsSource)], showDuplicates. Candidates are recomputed through `SafeHooks.useMemo(mergeStateKey)` over `applyMergeState(...)`, so merges are reflected locally without a refetch; never call onRefresh after a merge (that caused flicker, PR #77). `handleMerge` calls `ctx.api.client.mergeExpenses(survivorId, MergeExpenses.Request(loserId, keepDetailsFrom))` and then updates state with functional setters (`setDeletedIds(_ + id)`). Use functional setters for any async or bulk update. The merge confirm dialog is `mergeDialog`, with text from `mergeSummary`. The toolbar button "Possible duplicates (N)" toggles the panel, so the feature is already reachable.
- Server: server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/ExpensesRepository.scala `merge(survivorId, loserId, userId, keepDetailsFrom)` runs inside `database.withTransaction`, wrapped in `ConstraintViolations.translating(...)`. `validateMerge` returns `Either[MergeError, ValidatedMerge]`, and failures are thrown as `RuntimeException(e.message)`, which the controller's handleRequest turns into an error response that tests match with `.expectError` + `must include(message)`. Guard helpers: `BankStatementRowDAO.existsForExpense(id, userId)`, `ReceiptDAO.findByExpenseId(id, userId): Option[Receipt]`, `RefundDAO.reassignExpense(from, to, userId, now)`, and `ExpenseDAO.delete(id, userId)` (throws if no row was deleted). `MergeError` is an enum in the companion object. The controller (server/src/main/scala/controllers/ExpensesController.scala) and `MergeExpensesAction` just pass arguments through; no endpoint or model change is needed for this epic.
- Tests: server/src/test/scala/controllers/ExpensesControllerSpec.scala, the "POST /expenses/:id/merge" block (~line 406), with helpers `createRequest()`, `fullSplit(amount)`, `linkToNewRow(userId, expenseId)(using client)`, `createLinkedReceipt(userId, expenseId)`, `buildClient()`, `createVerifyLoginUser(tokenGenerator)`. Web: web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/utils/ExpenseDuplicateDetectorSpec.scala (an `expense(amount, date, merchantId, hasRow, hasReceipt)` builder, plus `survivor` and `loser` helpers; add an `orphan` helper). web/src/test/.../expenses/ExpenseDuplicatesPanelSpec.scala renders inside `BrowserRouter` with jsdom and a `null.asInstanceOf[API]` ctx, which is valid only because View receipt isn't rendered when receiptFilenames is empty. It has `clickButton(label)` (asserts exactly one match) and `lastLineOf(columnTitle)`. ExpensesPageSpec tests the pure `ExpenseList` helpers.
- Checkbox pattern: `(mui.Checkbox.checked(b).indeterminate(x).size("small").onChange((_, checked) => ...): ReactElement)`, as in BulkExpenseCreationPage.scala:442 and BankStatementReviewRow.scala:244.

Conventions:
- Name same-typed arguments at call sites (reviewer rule from PR #76), e.g. `merge(survivorId = ..., loserId = ...)`.
- Every query on user-owned data includes user_id.
- Frontend: no object-level `val` holding React elements; use `def` for elements reused in one tree. No `js.Dynamic` or `asInstanceOf` in components (the spec's null API is fine). Use theme CSS vars (`var(--lc-...)`), not hex colors. No setTimeout hacks.
- Tests: spec subject strings name the method only, not the class (RULE-TE-001). Use `= uninitialized`, not `= _`.
- Verification: run targeted `sbt "testOnly *XSpec"` or `CI=true sbt Test/compile`. Don't run the full `sbt test`. Web tests need Node 24 on PATH (the default shell node is v16, and yarn install fails without it). Run `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt` before finishing.

Non-obvious:
- `GetExpenses` doesn't expose refunds. A plain delete of an orphan could break refund links, which is why orphans go through merge, where refunds are reassigned to the survivor.
- After a receipt merge the survivor holds a receipt. It no longer qualifies as a receipt-shape survivor but can still be an orphan-shape survivor; that's intended.
- Unambiguous candidates share no expense ids, so running bulk merges in order never conflicts.
